narratives.Description: Address actionable review findings on deftai/directive#6307 concerning filesystem path canonicalization and protected-write authorization classification.
narratives.Overview: Keep existing path-comparison behavior while exposing when realpath resolution fell back. Keep GitHub CLI option parsing aligned with normalized tokens, cover accepted value forms, and document the user-visible protected-write behavior clearly.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1) Expose canonical, partial, and fallback path-resolution status and test a realpath failure. 2) Normalize GitHub CLI value-flag comparisons consistently and test repository flags before mutating verbs. 3) Verify protected-output flag spellings against the read-only proof and add regression tests for any actionable gap. 4) Rewrite the Unreleased changelog entry in user-visible terms.

narrative.Acceptance: A caller can distinguish fully canonicalized paths, paths with missing suffixes, and realpath fallback; sameFilesystemPath retains its existing string-comparison behavior.
narrative.Traces: PR #6307 review 5926047497 and latest SLizard review 5931238688.

narrative.Acceptance: GitHub CLI repository value flags are parsed using normalized tokens, supported attached forms cannot hide a mutating resource verb, and read-only output-destination checks have regression coverage for supported flag forms.
The Unreleased changelog entry leads with the protected-write authorization behavior and safe inspection behavior rather than implementation mechanics.

clauses.text: Path comparison keeps its current fallback result while exposing whether realpath fully succeeded, resolved only the existing prefix, or failed; tests deterministically cover the failure state.

GitHub CLI repository option parsing consistently uses normalized tokens and classifies supported separated and attached repository values before mutation verbs; output-destination proof forms are tested against supported commands.
The Unreleased changelog describes the user-visible protection against indirect writes while noting that read-only inspection remains allowed.
